info.title: Orchestra Agents API
info.description: Endpoints for Orchestra's AI agents: the agents, their skills and sessions.

get.description: List the avatars an agent can use: Orchestra's stock avatars and those uploaded to the workspace the credential resolves to. Pass an entry's `path` as `avatar_path` when creating or updating an agent. `url` is a short-lived link to the image, and is omitted for an uploaded avatar that is still being scanned for malware.

post.description: Start a session with an agent and send it a first prompt. The agent replies asynchronously: this returns once the prompt is queued, and the reply is read from `GET /sessions/{session_id}/history/messages`. Without `incidentId` the session is the caller's own, so it needs an OAuth token and an API key gets 400. With `incidentId` it is the incident's, visible across the workspace, and an incident's open session takes the prompt instead of a new one starting. Needs a grant to run the agent, and to view the incident when `incidentId` is set.

get.description: Read a page of an agent session's messages, a whole number of complete turns at a time, oldest first. Pass exactly one of `before_sequence_id` or `after_sequence_id`. Every message carries a `sequenceId` of the form `<unix-milliseconds>-<counter>`, and sequence IDs order as strings. So `before_sequence_id` set to the current time in milliseconds reads the latest turns, and `after_sequence_id=0` reads from the start of the session. Page back with `nextBeforeSequenceId` while `hasPreviousPage` is true, and forward with `nextAfterSequenceId` while `hasNextPage` is true. A turn still in progress is left out until it completes. Returns 404 for a session the caller cannot see, and 403 for one whose agent the caller cannot view. A session started by a user in the Orchestra UI is visible to that user alone, so an API key never sees one. Sessions started for a task run or an incident are visible to everyone in the workspace who can view the agent.

get.description: Stream an agent session as Server-Sent Events: the last three turns are replayed, including any turn still in progress, then new messages are sent as the session produces them. The stream closes after ten minutes without a new message. Every message carries a `sequenceId` of the form `<unix-milliseconds>-<counter>`, and sequence IDs order as strings. To read a session's replies without holding a connection open, use `GET /sessions/{session_id}/history/messages`. Returns 404 for a session the caller cannot see, and 403 for one whose agent the caller cannot view. A session started by a user in the Orchestra UI is visible to that user alone, so an API key never sees one. Sessions started for a task run or an incident are visible to everyone in the workspace who can view the agent.

get.description:
Retrieve the input and output tokens spent by agent sessions in the account, summed across every agent and LLM connection, as totals for the period and in consecutive time buckets. A session counts towards the bucket it was created in.

<Note>
  `time_from` and `time_to` are optional. If neither is provided, the API returns the last 30 days. If only one is provided, the period is the 30 days after `time_from` or before `time_to`. The maximum period per request is 366 days, and `time_from` cannot be earlier than 2023-01-01.
</Note>

Requires permission to view account settings.

parameters.name: time_from

schema.description: Start of the period as an ISO 8601 datetime with a UTC offset, for example `2026-09-01T00:00:00Z`.
schema.title: Time From

parameters.description: Start of the period as an ISO 8601 datetime with a UTC offset, for example `2026-09-01T00:00:00Z`.

parameters.name: time_to

schema.description: End of the period as an ISO 8601 datetime with a UTC offset, for example `2026-10-01T00:00:00Z`.
schema.title: Time To

parameters.description: End of the period as an ISO 8601 datetime with a UTC offset, for example `2026-10-01T00:00:00Z`.

schema.description: Length of each time bucket in minutes. Defaults to 1440 (one day); minimum 15, maximum 527040 (366 days).
